papers.title: Progress in anticancer chemical constituents and pharmacological research of Carpesium cernuum L. (Review).
papers.abstract: The present study aimed to systematically review the anticancer chemical constituents, pharmacological effects, and molecular targets of Carpesium cernuum L., clarify the molecular network of its anticancer mechanisms, summarize the research achievements and limitations and provide a scientific reference for its development and utilization, the research and development of novel anticancer drugs, and clinical applications. Through literature collation and experimental data integration, the chemical constituents of C. cernuum were classified and identified, and with the aid of in vitro cell expe
papers.summary: This review compiles the anticancer chemical constituents of the medicinal plant Carpesium cernuum L., cataloging its bioactive compounds and their pharmacological effects and molecular targets. It integrates literature and experimental data to map the molecular network underlying the plant's anticancer mechanisms, while noting current research limitations. The work aims to provide a reference for developing novel anticancer drugs from this plant source.

papers.title: Lessons From CABBI: Advancing Vegetative Oil Production in C4 Crops Through a Vertically Integrated DBTL Framework.
papers.abstract: The global demand for renewable liquid fuels and biobased chemicals has intensified interest in engineering high-biomass C4 grasses to accumulate triacylglycerol (TAG) in vegetative tissues. Achieving this goal requires coordinated solutions across molecular biology, crop science, chemical engineering, and life cycle assessment, disciplines that rarely operate within a single research program. The Center for Advanced Bioenergy and Bioproducts Innovation (CABBI) was established to provide this integration through a Design-Build-Test-Learn (DBTL) framework applied to three C4 feedstocks: sacchar
papers.summary: This paper describes how the CABBI center used a vertically integrated Design-Build-Test-Learn framework to engineer C4 grasses (such as sorghum, sugarcane, and miscanthus) to accumulate triacylglycerol (oil) in vegetative tissues rather than just seeds. By coordinating molecular biology, crop science, chemical engineering, and life cycle assessment within a single program, the authors show how such cross-disciplinary integration can accelerate progress toward renewable liquid fuels and biobased chemicals. The work offers lessons on organizing large-scale bioenergy engineering efforts around iterative DBTL cycles.

papers.title: Impact of EEG-related HPO terms on phenotype-driven variant prioritization in pediatric epilepsy.
papers.abstract: The Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) is a standardized resource of hierarchically organized phenotypic terms used for deep phenotyping, both in research and diagnosis. In our study, we aimed to investigate how the specificity of EEG-related HPO terms may impact phenotype and gene scoring and prioritization.
papers.summary: This study examines how the specificity of EEG-related Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) terms affects phenotype-driven gene scoring and variant prioritization in pediatric epilepsy. The authors investigate whether using more or less specific EEG terms changes the ranking of candidate genes, providing guidance for deep phenotyping in clinical genomics.

papers.title: LACA: a cross-species single-cell resource for exploring longevity and aging-associated cellular and molecular programs.
papers.abstract: Different species can have various maximum lifespans, some with exceptional longevity, yet the underlying cellular and molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Despite rapid advances in single-cell transcriptomics, resources that systematically connect single-cell gene expression profiles to species lifespan are limited. We hereby present the Longevity & Aging Cell Atlas (LACA), a database that integrates single-cell transcriptomic datasets across 134 species with their maximum lifespans. LACA includes over 148 million cells with 190 annotated cell types from single-cell datasets. LACA a
papers.summary: LACA is a new database that integrates single-cell transcriptomic datasets from 134 species with information on their maximum lifespans, covering over 148 million cells and 190 annotated cell types. It enables researchers to compare cellular and molecular programs across species to uncover mechanisms underlying longevity and aging. The resource addresses the lack of systematic connections between single-cell gene expression and species lifespan.

papers.title: PRGdb 5.0: a multi-layered resource for plant resistance gene discovery and exploration.
papers.abstract: Plant Resistance Genes database (PRGdb) 5.0 (https://prgdb.org/prgdb5/) is a major update of the PRGdb, designed to expand plant disease resistance gene resources within a unified web platform. The release incorporates predictions for 97 plant proteomes and adds 288, 315 new putative resistance-associated proteins, bringing the database to 874,967 candidate resistance proteins from 279 plant proteomes. The curated reference collection increased from 199 to 462 experimentally supported resistance proteins. To complement domain-based classification, the platform introduces an AI-assisted priorit
papers.summary: PRGdb 5.0 is a major update to the Plant Resistance Genes database, expanding it to 874,967 candidate resistance proteins across 279 plant proteomes, including 288,315 newly predicted resistance-associated proteins. The curated reference set of experimentally supported resistance proteins grew from 199 to 462, and the platform adds AI-assisted prioritization to complement domain-based classification. This provides plant biologists with a unified resource for discovering and exploring disease resistance genes.

papers.title: The mOTUs-db in 2027: linking taxonomy, genome-encoded function, and biogeography across environments.
papers.abstract: A molecular understanding of microbial communities requires linking taxonomic composition to the genome-resolved functional potential of member taxa. However, this integration remains challenging since representative genomes from cultivated strains are unavailable. Here, we present a new release of the mOTUs database, which extends genome coverage of underexplored environments and enriches its 3.9 million genome collection with functional annotations. Samples are annotated with a new hierarchical environmental ontology and geographic coordinates, supporting customizable sample grouping and bio
papers.summary: The mOTUs database has been updated to version 2027, expanding genome coverage for understudied environments and adding functional annotations to its 3.9 million genomes. It now includes a hierarchical environmental ontology and geographic coordinates for samples, enabling customizable grouping and linking of taxonomy, genome-encoded function, and biogeography. This resource helps researchers connect microbial community composition to functional potential even when cultured representatives are lacking.

papers.title: A multi-layer, multi-species graph-based framework for comparative analysis of sRNA-mediated regulation.
papers.abstract: Small RNAs (sRNAs) are central post-transcriptional regulators of bacterial gene expression, yet their evolutionary dynamics remain difficult to resolve due to limited sequence conservation. While sequence-homologous sRNAs can retain or diverge in function, unrelated sRNAs may independently evolve to regulate similar biological processes, making functional conservation invisible to sequence-based approaches. Here, we present a multi-layer, multi-species graph-based framework that integrates experimentally detected sRNA-messenger RNA interactions, orthology relationships, functional annotations
papers.summary: The authors present a graph-based computational framework that integrates experimentally detected sRNA–mRNA interactions, orthology relationships, and functional annotations across multiple bacterial species to enable comparative analysis of sRNA-mediated regulation. This approach addresses the difficulty of resolving sRNA evolutionary dynamics when sequence conservation is limited, allowing detection of functional conservation even among unrelated sRNAs that regulate similar processes.

papers.title: CellStressDB: an AI-powered database of cellular responses to physical stressors.
papers.abstract: Physical stressors profoundly influence cellular behavior by triggering coordinated stress-response programs that regulate signaling, gene expression, metabolism, and cell fate. Here, we present CellStressDB (https://cellstressdb.omic.tech), an AI-powered database for exploring cellular responses to physical stressors. The current release contains data from 131 transcriptomic studies, with 2 364 816 cell and 1205 bulk sample observations from human and mouse across nine physical-stress classes and 21 tissue categories. Data and analyses are organized into 2848 indexed analysis entries across 7
papers.summary: CellStressDB is a new AI-powered database that compiles transcriptomic data on how cells respond to physical stressors, covering 131 studies with over 2.3 million single-cell and 1,205 bulk observations from human and mouse across nine stress classes and 21 tissue categories. It organizes these data into 2,848 indexed analysis entries, providing a centralized resource for exploring stress-response programs in signaling, gene expression, metabolism, and cell fate.

papers.title: A Graded Immune-Cell-Resolved cis-eQTL Mendelian Randomisation Screen Across Systemic Lupus Erythematosus and Related Immune Phenotypes.
papers.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a genetically complex autoimmune disease. Whole-blood expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) analyses capture average regulatory effects across leukocytes, whereas SLE involves immune processes that depend on cell context. Therefore, a cell-resolved screen requires rigorous verification of instrument identity, allele orientation, and the multiple-testing denominator before biological interpretation.
papers.summary: This paper presents a cell-type-resolved cis-eQTL Mendelian randomisation screen to identify gene regulatory effects underlying systemic lupus erythematosus and related immune phenotypes. The authors emphasise rigorous verification of instrument identity, allele orientation, and multiple-testing correction before biological interpretation, addressing the limitations of whole-blood eQTL analyses that average regulatory effects across leukocytes.

papers.title: PDBe in 2027: integrating literature annotations, molecular dynamics data, and AI-ready access.
papers.abstract: The Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe; pdbe.org) provides open access to experimentally determined biomacromolecular structures and enriches these data with biological and functional context. Here, we describe recent developments that expand the information connected to PDB structures and introduce new ways for researchers and computational tools to access it. Literature integration has been extended to additional open-access publications, substantially increasing the availability of residue-level annotations mined from the scientific literature. Cross-links to molecular dynamics simulations i
papers.summary: PDBe has expanded its structural database by integrating residue-level annotations mined from more open-access literature, adding cross-links to molecular dynamics simulation data, and introducing AI-ready access methods. These updates make experimentally determined biomacromolecular structures more richly contextualized and easier for both researchers and computational tools to use.

papers.title: ONITH: An ontology-based non-clinical integration and term harmonization pipeline for data reuse in 3R.
papers.abstract: Animal studies continue to play a critical role in drug development as they uniquely capture the physiological complexity required to elucidate drug mechanisms and safety profiles. However, in alignment with the 3R principles (Reduce, Refine, Replace), there is a growing ethical and regulatory commitment to minimizing animal use. As part of this effort, the reuse of existing data has emerged as a potential strategy to support the transition toward more data-driven approaches in drug development, a direction that is increasingly supported by regulatory authorities as a viable alternative to ani
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.summary: ONITH is a pipeline that integrates non-clinical animal study data and harmonizes terminology using ontologies, aiming to make existing animal data more reusable in line with the 3R principles (Reduce, Refine, Replace). By standardizing terms across heterogeneous sources, it supports data-driven drug development while reducing the need for new animal experiments.

papers.title: Multi-omics-constrained kinetic models quantify pathway rewiring and predict metabolic vulnerabilities in BRCA1-deficient ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Time-resolved, network-wide consequences of cancer metabolic reprogramming remain poorly understood. We built multi-omics-constrained, near-genome-scale kinetic ensembles for isogenic BRCA1 wild-type and BRCA1-mutant ovarian cancer cells. Covering over 2,100 reactions, the ensembles enabled uncertainty-quantified simulations of nutrient, metabolite, and enzyme perturbations. Metabolic control analysis identified 28 enzyme-mediated vulnerabilities; 24 are linked to experimental or approved DrugBank compounds, whereas four lack documented drug associations. Independent DepMap data supported a su
papers.summary: The authors built near-genome-scale kinetic models of metabolism (over 2,100 reactions) constrained by multi-omics data for isogenic BRCA1 wild-type and BRCA1-mutant ovarian cancer cells, enabling uncertainty-quantified simulation of metabolic perturbations. Metabolic control analysis revealed 28 enzyme-level vulnerabilities, 24 of which map to existing or approved drugs, and independent DepMap data supported the predictions. The work shows that multi-omics-constrained kinetic modeling can quantify pathway rewiring and prioritize metabolic drug targets in a genotype-specific manner.

papers.title: PANTHER: the protein tree and function resource in 2027.
papers.abstract: PANTHER (Protein ANalysis THrough Evolutionary Relationships) is a comprehensive resource of phylogenetic trees of protein-coding gene families. Trees are manually annotated with Gene Ontology (GO) terms describing how protein functional characteristics were gained and lost over time along tree branches, and these evolutionary models are used to create GO annotations for protein-coding genes. Orthologs, paralogs, and xenologs are assigned based on the trees. Here, we describe updates to the PANTHER resource since our previous published report in 2022. Since that time, the content of the databa
papers.summary: PANTHER is a database of phylogenetic trees for protein-coding gene families, with branches manually annotated with Gene Ontology terms that model how protein functions evolved over time. These evolutionary models are used to propagate GO annotations to genes and to classify orthologs, paralogs, and xenologs. This paper reports updates to the resource since its 2022 publication, including expanded database content.

papers.title: PIANO enables generative modeling of gene expression and scales multi-omics integration to 100 million cells.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA technologies enable the routine acquisition of transcriptomic atlases. However, these molecular profiles are influenced by overlapping sources of variation. Since these covariates confound comparisons, data integration is the first step in most analyses. Three challenges remain: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells, and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. To address these challenges, we developed PIANO, probabilistic inference autoencoder networks for multi-omics, a deep learning framework whose central feature is a generative model of ge
papers.summary: PIANO is a deep learning framework that uses a generative model of gene expression to integrate single-cell multi-omics data. It addresses three key challenges: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells (demonstrated up to 100 million), and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. This enables more accurate comparisons across large-scale transcriptomic atlases.

papers.title: gcPathogen 2.0: an expanded multi-omics database advancing global pathogen surveillance and One Health research.
papers.abstract: Launched in 2024, gcPathogen established a critical foundation for the genomic surveillance of human pathogens. Here, we present gcPathogen 2.0, a major multi-omics update designed to address key analytical bottlenecks, including the integration of genomic and transcriptional profiles, systematic tracking of cross-habitat distribution, and large-scale discovery of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs). This release expands coverage from 1134 to 1506 pathogenic species, spanning 557 bacteria, 508 fungi, 258 viruses, and 183 parasites, and increases total genomic records past 2.3 million. By incorporati
papers.summary: gcPathogen 2.0 is a major expansion of a pathogen genomic surveillance database, growing from 1,134 to 1,506 pathogenic species and exceeding 2.3 million genomic records. The update adds transcriptional profiles, cross-habitat distribution tracking, and large-scale antimicrobial peptide discovery, supporting One Health research across bacteria, fungi, viruses, and parasites.

papers.title: Metabolomics Subcenter (Met-SC): an integrated metabolomics database and analysis platform.
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of metabolomics data has increased the need for integrated storage, analysis, and reuse. Here, we present Metabolomics Subcenter (Met-SC) V1.0 (https://metabolomics.dicp.ac.cn/), an integrated database and platform for standardized data deposition, spectral-resource management, online analysis, and disease-focused knowledge mining. The deposition framework captures project, sample, pretreatment, and instrument metadata across chromatographic, capillary electrophoresis-mass spectrometry, and nuclear magnetic resonance workflows. Met-SC contains 7  756  867 reference spectra ass
papers.summary: Met-SC is a new integrated metabolomics database and analysis platform that standardizes data deposition, manages spectral resources, and supports online analysis and disease-focused knowledge mining. It captures detailed metadata across LC-MS, CE-MS, and NMR workflows and contains over 7.7 million reference spectra. The resource aims to facilitate storage, reuse, and analysis of the rapidly growing metabolomics data.

papers.title: Conversational Multi-Agentic Network-Driven Disease Module Identification and Drug Repurposing Prediction With ChatDRex: Platform Development Study.
papers.abstract: Repurposing approved drugs offers a time- and cost-effective alternative to traditional drug development. However, in silico prediction of repurposing candidates is challenging and requires the effective collaboration of specialists in various fields, including pharmacology, medicine, biology, and bioinformatics. Fragmented, specialized algorithms and tools often address only narrow aspects of the overall problem. Heterogeneous, unstructured data landscapes require the expertise of specialized users. Hence, diverse data sources might not integrate smoothly across workflows.
papers.summary: ChatDRex is a conversational multi-agent platform that integrates disease module identification and drug repurposing prediction by coordinating specialized AI agents over heterogeneous biomedical data and networks. It aims to lower the barrier to in silico repurposing by letting users interact in natural language while agents handle data integration and analysis. The work is presented as a platform development study, so its main contribution is the system design rather than a validated repurposing discovery.

papers.title: InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2027.
papers.abstract: InterPro (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro) is a freely accessible resource for the classification of protein sequences. It integrates predictive models, known as signatures, from multiple member databases to classify sequences into families and to predict the presence of domains and functionally important sites. The InterPro database provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, ensuring extensive coverage of UniProtKB, the standard repository of protein sequences, and includes mapping to several other major resources, such as Gene Ontology, the Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe),
papers.summary: InterPro is a freely accessible database that classifies protein sequences by integrating predictive models (signatures) from multiple member databases to assign sequences to families and predict domains and functional sites. The 2027 update provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, giving extensive coverage of UniProtKB and linking to resources such as Gene Ontology and PDBe. This makes it a central reference for protein function annotation across the life sciences.

papers.title: Integration of single-cell multi-omic data with graph-based topic modelling.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in single-cell biology enable the profiling of multiple molecular layers, such as the transcriptome, epigenome, and surface proteins, within a single cell. Tackling the complexity of these data from multiple perspectives allows researchers to gain the most comprehensive insights into cellular biological properties. Here, we propose a graph-based topic modelling method called bionSBM. Our method leverages well-known community-detection methods for multipartite graphs and the interpretability of topic modelling to cluster and explain high-dimensional, sparse, and noisy single-cel
papers.summary: The paper introduces bionSBM, a graph-based topic modelling method for integrating single-cell multi-omic data (transcriptome, epigenome, surface proteins). It combines community-detection on multipartite graphs with topic modelling to cluster and interpret high-dimensional, sparse, and noisy single-cell data. The approach aims to provide a more comprehensive view of cellular properties by jointly analyzing multiple molecular layers.

papers.title: Functional Analysis of GarCIPK8 from Gossypium aridum Conferring Salt Stress Tolerance in Gossypium hirsutum.
papers.abstract: Soil salinization is a major abiotic stress factor restricting global agricultural production. The CBL-CIPK signaling network, comprising calcineurin B-like proteins (CBLs) and CBL-interacting protein kinases (CIPKs), plays a critical role in plant adaptation to salt stress. Here, we focused on GarCIPK8, a CIPK gene previously isolated from the diploid wild cotton Gossypium aridum, and generated its overexpressing transgenic lines in G. hirsutum through Agrobacterium-mediated transformation. Under 300 mmol/L NaCl treatment, transgenic plants showed markedly enhanced growth performance, with gr
papers.summary: The authors transferred GarCIPK8, a salt-responsive kinase gene from a wild diploid cotton species, into cultivated upland cotton and found that overexpressing lines grew markedly better under high-salinity (300 mM NaCl) conditions. This suggests that the CBL-CIPK signaling pathway can be harnessed through transgenic approaches to improve salt tolerance in an important crop.

papers.title: Crystalline silica particles exposure modulated miRNA expression profiles in human macrophage-like THP-1 cells.
papers.abstract: Occupational and environmental exposure to crystalline silica particles is a major global health concern linked to silicosis, pulmonary fibrosis, autoimmune disease, and lung cancer. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) regulate gene expression post-transcriptionally and are emerging as potential effect biomarkers of exposure in human biomonitoring studies. To identify intracellular and extracellular miRNAs responses to silica-particle exposure in human THP-1 derived macrophages, differentiated THP-1 derived macrophages were exposed to 0-300 µg/mL crystalline silica particles for 24 h. Cytotoxicity was assessed
papers.summary: This study exposed human macrophage-like THP-1 cells to crystalline silica particles and profiled changes in microRNA expression both inside cells and released extracellularly. The findings identify miRNA signatures associated with silica exposure, suggesting these small RNAs could serve as biomarkers for monitoring occupational silica exposure and early lung injury.

papers.title: Development of a Knowledge Map for Managing Symptoms of Graft-Versus-Host Disease in Patients Undergoing Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation.
papers.abstract: Graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) remains a critical complication affecting patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), with multifaceted symptoms requiring systematic management. Current clinical practices lack structured tools to guide nurses in addressing GVHD-related symptoms across diverse organ systems. This review aims to synthesize evidence on GVHD symptom management to construct a knowledge graph, enhancing nursing interventions and improving patient outcomes.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on managing symptoms of graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation to build a knowledge graph for nursing interventions. The goal is to provide a structured tool that helps nurses address GVHD symptoms across multiple organ systems, addressing a gap in current clinical practice.

papers.title: Cutibacterium acnes induces T-cell extracellular traps with distinct proteome programs.
papers.abstract: Cutibacterium acnes is a common skin commensal associated with acne pathogenesis. In this study, we investigated whether acne-associated (denoted as CA) (HL043PA1) and healthy skin-associated (denoted as CH) (HL110PA3) C acnes strains differentially induce extracellular traps (ETs) in human neutrophils (neutrophil ETs) and T helper 17 cells (T-cell ETs [TETs]) and defined their proteomic and functional properties. Both strains triggered rapid ET release from neutrophils and T helper 17 cells. However, whereas neutrophil ETs displayed a conserved proteomic profile regardless of the strain, TETs
papers.summary: This study shows that both acne-associated and healthy skin-associated strains of Cutibacterium acnes trigger rapid extracellular trap release from human neutrophils and Th17 cells. While neutrophil extracellular traps had a conserved proteomic profile regardless of strain, T-cell extracellular traps induced by the two strains showed distinct proteomic programs, suggesting strain-specific functional consequences in skin immunity.

papers.title: Reactive astrocyte subpopulations with high Gfap and C4b expression in different Alzheimer's disease mouse models: Single-cell nuclear transcriptome analysis.
papers.abstract: Understanding the cellular landscape underlying the heterogeneity of Alzheimer’s disease and the cell type-specific molecular perturbations is essential for identifying novel, targeted therapeutic strategies. However, previous bulk transcriptomic studies have failed to capture the unique contributions of individual cell populations to the early pathogenesis of the disease, and the functional diversity of key cell types in driving Alzheimer’s disease progression remains insufficiently characterized. In this study, we examined transcriptional changes in hippocampal tissue during early Alzheimer’
papers.summary: This study used single-nucleus RNA sequencing to profile hippocampal tissue from multiple Alzheimer's disease mouse models at early disease stages, focusing on reactive astrocyte heterogeneity. The authors identified distinct reactive astrocyte subpopulations characterized by high expression of Gfap and C4b, revealing cell-type-specific transcriptional changes that bulk transcriptomics had obscured. The findings highlight conserved and model-specific astrocyte states that may contribute to early AD pathogenesis.

papers.title: Reframing QSP: AI-Driven Multi-Modal Data as a New Measurement Layer.
papers.abstract: Quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) provides a mechanistic framework for integrating biological and pharmacological knowledge in drug development. Simultaneously, advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly in multi-modal data analysis, are transforming how biological information is derived. I argue that AI should not be viewed as a data integration tool, but as a new layer of quantitative measurement generation. This reframing positions QSP as a foundational model of biology, used here in a conceptual rather than technical sense, and AI as a source of quantitative inputs.
papers.summary: This perspective argues that AI-driven multi-modal data analysis should be reframed not as a tool for integrating data into quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) models, but as a new layer that generates quantitative measurements. Under this view, QSP serves as a conceptual foundational model of biology while AI supplies the quantitative inputs, potentially reshaping how mechanistic drug-development models are built and parameterized.

papers.title: PDBe-SIFTS: An open-source tool for Structure Integration with Function, Taxonomy, and Sequences, featuring improved alignment, scoring scheme, and accelerated search.
papers.abstract: Structure integration with function, taxonomy and sequences (SIFTS) provides residue-level mappings between UniProt Knowledgebase sequences and Protein Data Bank structures and has historically been generated through internal Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe) pipelines. Here, PDBe-SIFTS is presented as a fully open-source, locally deployable implementation of this mapping framework. The pipeline combines fast, scalable sequence search using MMseqs2, an improved bounded scoring scheme for ranking candidate mappings, and residue-level mapping refinement based on backbone connectivity. PDBe-SIFT
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: PDBe-SIFTS is a new open-source, locally deployable tool that maps UniProt protein sequences to PDB structures at residue-level resolution. It improves on the original SIFTS pipeline by using MMseqs2 for fast sequence search, a better scoring scheme for ranking candidate mappings, and refinement based on backbone connectivity. This makes high-quality structure-function mapping accessible to any lab without relying on internal PDBe infrastructure.

papers.title: EXPERT: A practical and forward-looking guide to capturing protein expression and purification metadata to develop machine learning models.
papers.abstract: As machine learning (ML) becomes increasingly important in protein engineering, synthetic biology, and bioprocess optimization, the lack of consistent, complete, and standardized experimental reporting remains a major barrier to building effective models. EXPERT (EXpression and Purification Experimental Reporting Template) defines a structured framework for capturing protein expression and purification data across the community, to increase reproducibility across laboratories and support downstream ML applications. We propose here the essential data that should be recorded during expression an
papers.summary: EXPERT is a proposed standardized template for recording protein expression and purification metadata, addressing the inconsistency and incompleteness of current experimental reporting that hinders machine learning model development. By defining a structured framework for capturing essential data across laboratories, it aims to improve reproducibility and enable downstream ML applications in protein engineering and bioprocess optimization.

papers.title: Single-cell chromatin accessibility atlas decodes bone development, diseases, and regeneration.
papers.abstract: Bone development, homeostasis, and regeneration are governed by complex, dynamic gene regulatory programs, and these processes are disrupted in numerous skeletal diseases. The epigenetic landscape-particularly chromatin accessibility-dictates transcription factor binding and gene expression, which fundamentally shape bone cell fate and function. In recent years, single-cell chromatin accessibility technologies, most notably single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq), have revolutionized bone epigenome research and enabled single-cell resolution dissect
papers.summary: This review describes how single-cell chromatin accessibility profiling, especially scATAC-seq, has been applied to bone biology, revealing the gene regulatory programs that control bone cell fate, development, homeostasis, and regeneration, and how these programs go awry in skeletal diseases. It synthesizes the emerging single-cell epigenomic atlas of bone and discusses its implications for understanding disease mechanisms and advancing regenerative strategies.

papers.title: Comparative Transcriptomic and Physiological Profiling Reveals Species-Associated Differences Across Five Duckweed Species.
papers.abstract: Duckweeds (Lemnaceae) are fast-growing aquatic monocots with potential for biomass production and phytoremediation, but baseline molecular and physiological differences among species remain poorly characterized. We assembled de novo transcriptomes of five duckweed species, Lemna minor, Lemna japonica, Lemna gibba, Landoltia punctata, and Lemna aequinoctialis, grown on basal Murashige and Skoog (MS) medium (three biological replicates per species), and evaluated for completeness with Benchmarking Universal Single-Copy Orthologs (BUSCO) against Viridiplantae, Embryophyta, and Liliopsida referenc
papers.summary: This study generated de novo transcriptome assemblies for five duckweed species and compared them alongside physiological measurements to identify species-specific molecular and phenotypic differences. The work provides a baseline resource for understanding variation among these fast-growing aquatic plants, which are candidates for biomass production and phytoremediation.

papers.title: A Traditional Chinese Medicine Knowledge Graph for Hypertension With Emotional Comorbidity: Development and Blinded Question-Answering Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) literature on hypertension with anxiety, depression, or insomnia contains descriptions of syndrome patterns, treatment principles, formulas, and herbs. A focused knowledge graph can organize these associations and their sources, but its contribution to generated answers requires separate evaluation.
papers.summary: This paper develops a focused knowledge graph that organizes Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) literature on hypertension with emotional comorbidities (anxiety, depression, insomnia), capturing syndrome patterns, treatment principles, formulas, and herbs with source attribution. It then evaluates the knowledge graph's contribution to generated answers through a blinded question-answering assessment. The work demonstrates a domain-specific approach to structuring TCM knowledge and assessing its utility in downstream QA systems.

papers.title: Integration of genotyping by sequencing and machine learning for genome-wide identification of informative markers for body weight in broiler chickens.
papers.abstract: Identifying associations between single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and economically important traits is fundamental to modern poultry breeding programs. However, genome-wide studies based on commercial high-density SNP arrays are often prohibitively expensive, particularly for large populations and in resource-limited settings. Therefore, this study employed a cost-effective genotyping-by-sequencing (GBS) approach combined with two ensemble machine learning algorithms, Random Forest (RF) and Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), to identify informative markers of body weight (BW) at hatch, 3 w
papers.summary: This study combined cost-effective genotyping-by-sequencing (GBS) with two ensemble machine learning methods, Random Forest and Gradient Boosting Machine, to identify informative SNP markers associated with body weight in broiler chickens at hatch and 3 weeks of age. The approach demonstrates that GBS plus ML can serve as a cheaper alternative to high-density SNP arrays for genome-wide association studies in poultry breeding. The work highlights candidate markers that could inform selection programs for growth traits.

papers.title: Dingent: A Configurable Agent Framework for Biological Database Retrieval and Integration.
papers.abstract: Natural-language retrieval across biological databases requires resource-specific tools, model instructions, and coordinated query steps. We present Dingent, an open-source agent framework that composes resource-specific tools into explicit multistep retrieval paths, integrating data-access plugins, configurable assistants, directed workflows, and web interfaces. Within this framework, developers expose resource functions as tools, administrators configure assistants and workflows, and users query the resulting application in natural language. We compared Dingent with a single-assistant tool-c
papers.summary: Dingent is an open-source framework that lets developers wrap biological database functions as tools and compose them into explicit, configurable multi-step retrieval workflows, with administrators configuring assistants and users querying in natural language. It provides data-access plugins, directed workflows, and web interfaces, and was benchmarked against a single-assistant tool-calling baseline. The work targets the practical engineering problem of coordinating resource-specific tools and instructions across heterogeneous biological databases.

papers.title: PhageLysData: an evidence-aware and AI-ready dataset of phage lytic enzymes and depolymerases.
papers.abstract: Bacteriophage lytic enzymes and depolymerases are relevant to phage biology, antimicrobial development, and protein engineering, but their sequence and annotation data remain dispersed across general databases, specialized resources, genome-centred collections, and prediction-oriented datasets. We present PhageLysData, an evidence-aware and AI-ready resource constructed through reproducible multisource integration, provenance tracking, and exact-sequence consolidation. The release integrates 807,366 source observations from seven primary resources into 759,105 unique exact-sequence entities, c
papers.summary: PhageLysData is a new curated database that consolidates phage lytic enzymes and depolymerases, integrating 807,366 source observations from seven primary resources into 759,105 unique exact-sequence entities. The resource emphasizes provenance tracking and evidence awareness, making it suitable for AI/ML applications in antimicrobial and protein engineering research. It addresses the fragmentation of phage enzyme data across general and specialized databases.

papers.title: Advancing FAIR data management through AI-assisted curation of morphological data matrices.
papers.abstract: Curation of biological and paleontological datasets is a labor-intensive process that requires standardization and validation to ensure data integrity. In particular, manual curation of datasets is prone to human errors such as typographical errors, inconsistent formatting, and incomplete metadata, which hinder reproducibility and compliance with Findability, Accessibility, Interoperability, and Reusability (FAIR) principles. Artificial Intelligence (AI) offers a transformative solution for enhancing research efficiency by automating data validation, improving accuracy, and streamlining curati
papers.summary: This paper presents an AI-assisted approach to curating morphological data matrices, automating validation tasks like detecting typographical errors, inconsistent formatting, and incomplete metadata. The authors argue this reduces manual curation burden and improves compliance with FAIR data principles, enhancing reproducibility in biological and paleontological datasets.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Multifaceted Toolkit for Antibacterial Drug Discovery against Resistance.
papers.abstract: How artificial intelligence (AI) can be rationally applied to antibacterial drug discovery and development to overcome antimicrobial resistance (AMR) remains insufficiently defined, particularly across different resistance mechanisms and translational stages. The global emergence and dissemination of AMR are compromising conventional antibacterial therapies, while slow antibiotic discovery, limited target diversity, and reliance on single-mechanism drug design further increase the risk of inadequate treatment options. papers.summary: This review argues that AI can serve as a multifaceted toolkit across the antibacterial drug discovery pipeline to combat antimicrobial resistance, spanning target identification, compound screening, and drug design. It emphasizes AI's strengths in integrating multi-omics data and recognizing complex patterns to address slow antibiotic discovery and limited target diversity. The paper frames AI application in the context of different resistance mechanisms and translational stages, though the abstract is truncated before detailing specific methods or results.
